chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Fletcher Henderson band personnel and what they taught him
summary: Sandy Williams, Joe Keyes, Claude Jones and others taught him big band playing on Henderson's difficult charts and pulled jokes on him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: 'I Hear Music', oh, it was just a great album, great album. And let's see, during that time I recorded with Benny Carter, and I did quite a few recordings with Fletcher during that time. I was speaking of Fletcher. I want to give you the personnel of this band. This was -- had a trombone player, Claude -- wait a minute. Sandy Williams, and we had a trumpet player, Joe Keyes, who was a great trumpet player. These guys were older than I was and they really taught me the business about band, you know, big band playing and a lot about music.

Well, firstly, Fletcher Henderson wrote the most difficult music that I'd ever read. You know, as a matter of fact he would write in G flat. These were unheard of keys. And these guys were superb musicians. You know, G flat, B natural, A natural. He would write in all these keys, of Stealing Apples, some of the tunes, and of -- Benny Goodman used his whole library when he formed his band. He just took Fletcher's whole library, the things that we were doing at that time, and this made -- this really made Benny.

But this band, coming back to this band, these guys were so full of fun, they used to pull jokes on me. I was like a youngster in the band, and they would stage fake fights and I would go and try to separate them and we just had a marvelous time. But as I say these were real pros. Pop Smith, a trumpet player who was a giant, was in this band. Jonah Jones was in this band.
Was the trombone player Claude Jones?

Claude Jones, that's it, yeah. Claude was very -- marvelous trombone player, marvelous person. But they would put me on, they would -- as I say they would fight and they would pretend that they were going to attack Fletcher, sometimes, and I'm trying to get -- keep them from going -- don't do that to Fletcher, Fletcher's such a marvelous --
